text:
Harper: Dropped a concise changelog + release note draft for the KV/prefix cache + batching work and the new Dedicated canary UI. Need fast sweep on: (1) public-facing Known Issues blurb, (2) snippets for py/js/ruby, (3) Private migration checklist, and (4) legal/marketing sign-off around bench numbers. Target publish tomorrow AM.

Diego: Link?

Harper: https://docs.redwood.ai/drafts/relnotes-cache-batching-canary (WIP)

Mei: I'll run snippets. Can we include a short Ruby example this time? Some customers use it in-platform. Keep v1 SDK shape; add short v0.9 compat note.

Finn: Known issue to call out: very small percentage of tokenization diffs when using 4-bit quant kernels on very long contexts. Add mitigation: re-tokenize with model vocab or run sensitive evals on full-precision. Keep exact percentages internal unless Legal clears it.

legal-bot: Heads-up: bench numbers require Legal review before public release. Recommend qualitative phrasing like "measurable per-route latency and cost improvements".

Diego: I'll do anchors + redirect sweep. Found one stale link to /docs/dedicated#canary-config -> now #canary-settings. I'll patch draft links.

Mei: Draft Python snippet (v1):
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="REDACTED")
resp = client.generate(
    model="redwood-optim-1",
    input="Summarize the changes",
    stream=True,
    options={"cache": {"kv_enabled": True}, "batch": {"max_tokens": 512}},
)
for chunk in resp.stream():
    print(chunk.text)
```
I'll add JS and Ruby equivalents.

Finn: Ruby snippet idea: show a minimal sync example and a streaming variant using the block/yield pattern.

Mei: Draft Ruby snippet:
```ruby
require "redwood"
client = Redwood::Client.new(api_key: ENV["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
resp = client.generate(
  model: "redwood-optim-1",
  input: "Summarize the changes",
  options: { cache: { kv_enabled: true }, batch: { max_tokens: 512 } }
)
puts resp.text
```
Add stream example below.

Diego: After my anchor fixes, can docs-bot run the linkcheck? Also update image alt text for accessibility on the Dedicated canary screenshot.

docs-bot: Linkcheck queued for 2026-03-24T21:00:00Z. Snippet linter scheduled.

Harper: Add a short migration checklist for Private customers: config rename (`kv_cache.enabled` -> `cache.kv_enabled`), helm override example, warmup curl to prime pinned variants, and a one-liner rollback for ops. Keep it concise.

Finn: Warmup curl draft:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://internal-infer.example/api/warmup" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-optim-1","variant":"pinned"}'
```
And rollback: `kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/inference-worker`

Mei: Snippet linter sometimes flags argument names across SDK versions. I'll include a small note: "Examples use v1 SDK; v0.9 users: use client.options namespace."

legal-bot: I'll queue a legal review. If you want to publish any numeric claim, add an internal-only callout or wait for sign-off.

publish-bot: Dry-run publish scheduled for 2026-03-24T22:00:00Z. Will run automated snippet linter and linkcheck.

Diego: One editorial ask: marketing prefers we avoid exact percent claims in public docs. Use the neutral blurb + link to a gated whitepaper if they want numbers.

Harper: OK we'll say "measurable per-route latency and cost improvements" publicly and keep the internal bench note with product docs for enterprise sales.

Mei: Pushing JS + Ruby snippets now. Will mark code comments for v0.9 compat.

Finn: Add "how to opt out" one-liner: `cache.kv_enabled=false` in the deployment spec for operators who want legacy behavior.

Harper: Thanks all. After linkcheck + linter and legal approval, I'll flip the draft to ready. If any blocker, ping @Harper or @Mei. :thumbsup:
